title: Introduce phase-aware trace-stitcher and token-anchor alert attenuation
author: Maya Sanchez
description:
Motivation: Long-tail token costs and backpressure effects were showing up as noisy alerts and fractured traces when requests hit kernel queueing or multi-stage prefetch logic. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a phase-aware Trace Stitcher that merges sparse spans across kernel/backpressure boundaries into a phase timeline (initialization, prefetch, generation, postprocess) and attaches token-anchor markers so logs and metrics can reliably attribute cost to token-phase slices; 2) a token-anchor alert attenuation layer which mutes low-confidence, short-lived cost spikes by correlating with phase stability and queue-depth.

What changed (high level): single continuous change description below.
- runtime/trace/stitcher: new component that ingests sampled spans, performs temporal alignment using request-clock anchors and kernel-queue offsets, and emits fused phase spans with token_range annotations.
- telemetry/metrics: added phase_token_cost, phase_token_p50_ms, phase_queue_depth gauges and a phase_stability score used by alert rules.
- observability/dashboards: new dashboard JSON (phase-cost-explorer.json) with stacked phase-cost sparklines, token-anchor timeline, and a queue-depth vs alert-probability panel.
- alerting/rules: token-anchor attenuation rule that reduces alert score when phase_stability < 0.6 or queue_depth shows transient spikes; integration with existing SLO suppression logic.
- docs: brief playbook section explaining how to interpret phase timelines and how attenuation interacts with canaries/rollouts.

Backward compatibility: the stitcher emits both legacy span links and the new fused phase spans when enabled; default behavior is disabled for tenants that rely on existing rollups (config flag observability.phase_stitcher.enabled=false).

Testing & rollout: unit tests for alignment heuristics and e2e smoke for dashboard rendering. Gradual rollout via feature flag with canary in prod for 10% of traffic, then ramp to 100% after 48h of metrics stability.

Notes: this is primarily an observability improvement (no functional model changes). Linear tickets ENG-1986 and ENG-2074 track follow-ups for per-tenant attenuation thresholds and UI filters.

review_conversation: Evan Tran (reviewer): Nice direction. Two questions: how do we avoid attribution doubling when legacy rollups are on? Can the stitcher operate on sampled traces only?

Maya Sanchez (author): Stitcher respects sampling flag; when legacy rollups are enabled we emit legacy links in addition to fused spans but the metrics emission is gated behind a tenant opt-in. Added config flag and unit tests to avoid double-counting.

Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Alert attenuation looks good, but we should expose per-tenant thresholds in the UI and make defaults conservative. Also add a dashboard panel that shows attenuation events over time so SREs can prove attenuation correctness.
Maya Sanchez (author): Added per-tenant threshold config, attenuation-events panel to dashboard, and a short doc section describing verification steps.
Lukas Müller (reviewer): CI flake in the integration dashboard smoke test — re-ran and it passed. Approving pending a minor comment about log level in annotator (changed to debug).
release_notes: Add phase-aware trace stitching and token-anchor attenuation to reduce noisy token-cost alerts and provide phase-level cost attribution. Disabled by default per-tenant; opt-in recommended for teams troubleshooting kernel/backpressure cost noise.
